text.tspan: with a single fused kernel. For example, the prefill Q and KV
projections (Section 3.1), the post-attention linear layer (Sec-
tion 3.1), and the QKV projection in MLA (Section 2.3) can be
fused. These fused kernels are shown in Figure 11. We measure
the kernel fusion’s effect on GPU utilization. For the MLA QKV
projection, fusion leads to a 1.25× reduction in GPU time. For
the prefill QKV projection in GPT-OSS, fusion leads to a 1.3×
speedup. For the post-attention linear layer, fusion leads to a
1.54× speedup. Fusion can also enable a single kernel launch,
reducing launch overhead (Chen et al., 2024; Shao et al., 2024;
Yang et al., 2024b).
We further find that the performance of the QKV projection
is significantly lower than the down projection in the GQA-
based models. This is due to the lower arithmetic intensity of
the QKV projection. We use Q4, K2, and V2 in the following
text to refer to the Q projection with the GQA ratio of 2, the
K projection, and the V projection, respectively.
We investigate the routing computation in MoE models and
find several inefficiencies: the top-k expert selection is
performed sequentially (limiting GPU utilization), the softmax
is computed redundantly per expert, and routing is not
overlapped with the following MoE GEMM. Our fused routing
kernel computes the top-k experts in parallel and overlaps
routing with the downstream GEMM.
We develop a GEMM with per-token-block scaling. Across all
MoE layers, our optimized MoE operations speed up 1.17× to
1.89× over the reference implementations.
... 512 experts in the second and third MoE layers. Across all
models and all MoE layers, our fused routing leads to 1.05×
to 1.90× speedup in the routing stage.
We identify several inefficiencies in MoE operations, including
the inefficiency in routing and MoE GEMM, and provide our
optimizations.
The current routing computation contains several inefficien-
cies. First, the computation of the top-k experts is not
parallel: the top-k experts are selected sequentially, which
limits GPU utilization. Our fused routing kernel computes the
top-k experts in a parallel manner. Second, the softmax is
computed redundantly: the softmax over the selected experts’
scores can be computed once rather than per expert. Third, the
routing computation and the following MoE GEMM are not
overlapped; we overlap them to improve utilization.
The MoE GEMM operates on a gathered, permuted activation
matrix, and the down / gate-up projections differ in shape and
arithmetic intensity. We compare our optimized MoE operations
with the reference implementations across all layers, reporting
the average kernel time per token where the top-8 experts are
selected from the 256 routed experts. Across the layers, our
MoE operations speed up 1.17× to 1.89×.
We can skip the routing computations during verification: only
the first token is sampled and the remaining tokens are
discarded. In practice the routing computations take ~38% time
on the sampled tokens. We can also skip the expert computation
for tokens in a sequence known to be discarded, saving ~17% on
the first token.
